name: Operations Control Tower
purpose: Turn monitoring alerts into incidents for a night operations team: group alerts by rules in code, find the root cause, set the severity, recommend one runbook step with the evidence, draft a status update for P1 and P2, answer operators' questions with sources, and make sure no change runs until the right people have approved it.
intended_users: Night operations engineers who watch the alerts
On-call engineers of the owning teams, who approve a change to their own service
The duty manager, who approves P1 incidents and tier-1 changes during the weekend change freeze
out_of_scope: Running any change on its own: every [CHANGE] step needs the approvals in policy section 5
Making or supporting decisions about people: scoring, ranking or monitoring engineers (that would make it high-risk under EU AI Act Annex III point 4)
Safety-critical control of physical or critical infrastructure
Anything outside the fictional company's own alerts, runbooks and policy
Handling real personal data or real secrets: the data in this repository is fictional

models.role: Large model: incident briefs (planner), summaries, drafts and hard questions
Small model: investigator turns, status-update drafts, simple runbook and policy look-ups
Test double: deterministic fake used by every test and the offline demo, never in production

sources: data/services.csv: the service catalogue with tiers, owners and dependencies
data/alerts.csv: 22 fictional alerts from 22 to 24 October 2026
data/incidents_history.csv: 16 past incidents and what fixed them
data/oncall.csv: on-call engineers (work email only is ever used)
docs/OPERATIONS_POLICY.md and docs/runbooks/RB-01 to RB-08: the rules and the steps
data.personal_data: Alert text can contain secrets (password=, token=) and an engineer's personal mobile number. They are hidden by Presidio and secret patterns before any model call, log line, trace, audit entry or screen. personal_mobile is stored in a separate table that the application's database connection cannot read; no tool, index or prompt is given it. Contacting a team is page_oncall(team), by team name only.
data.retention: Alert text is kept raw in the local SQLite file data/tower.db, which is rebuilt from the CSV files on demand; logs rotate at 2 MB with 2 backups. A real retention period is an open item (risk R06).

evaluation.scenarios_right: 10/10 scenarios right on grouping, root cause, severity, status, approvals, similar incident and flags with the real models (EVAL_REPORT.md); the rules alone score the same with no model
evaluation.runbook_steps_right: 10/10 runbook steps match with the real models, checked by code against the runbook before anyone sees them (EVAL_REPORT.md)
evaluation.attacks_stopped: 7/8 attacks stopped with the defences on; T08 (a paraphrased instruction in an alert) is an accepted risk, with the harm blocked by the Verifier and the approval step (SECURITY_FINDINGS.md)
evaluation.p95_seconds: 2.64 s p95 for /ask after routing and caching with the real models, against 4.13 s before (PERF_REPORT.md); the slow tail is the uncached large-model questions
evaluation.cost_per_1000_questions: $0.14 per 1,000 questions after routing and caching, against $1.12 before (PERF_REPORT.md)

limitations: A paraphrased instruction in an alert is not flagged (T08, accepted); it is stopped later by the runbook check and the approval step
Free-text answers can contain a wrong fact; the output check removes secrets, links and leaks but cannot verify facts, so facts with one right answer are answered from data with no model
The READ tools are simulated readings for the starter scenarios; no real system is touched and nothing real is changed
Approver identity is chosen from a list in this build; production needs single sign-on and a signed request
Evaluated on 10 scenarios and 30 questions of fictional data; results on real alerts are unknown
Presidio is configured for phone numbers, cards, IBANs and NHS numbers; names and addresses are not hidden
human_oversight: A person approves every [CHANGE] step: the owning team's on-call, plus the duty manager for P1 and for tier-1 changes in the weekend change freeze, with a written reason, two different people when two are needed, one step on one service, executed once. Unknown services and failed recommendations stop as NEEDS_PERSON. Status updates are drafts that a person sends. An incident waiting more than 15 minutes pages the duty manager. Every decision is in the audit trail.

risk_category.reason: Not a prohibited practice (Article 5) and not high-risk (not Annex I; not Annex III, because it decides nothing about people and is not a safety component of critical infrastructure). The Ask the tower chat interacts directly with people, so Article 50(1) applies and the screen says they are talking to an AI. See governance/classification.md.
